problems.title: Backblaze backup integrity cannot be verified

statement.task: Verify that a remote backup contains the expected files
statement.failure: The provider reports an inconsistency but does not expose a local-vs-remote hash comparison
statement.consequence: Millions of files may require manual checking or an expensive full restore without identifying the discrepancy

evidence.quote: The only official solution is to manually check all files (millions in my case).
There wouldn't be a way to compare hashes the way you describe in this case as that mechanism is simply not implemented
evidence.supports: Provider lacks the requested deterministic comparison

evidence.quote: Checks the files in the source and destination match.
evidence.supports: Conventional tools already implement this class of verification

counter_evidence: rclone, restic, Kopia, Arq, and Borg already provide deterministic verification patterns.

investigations.question: Does this require a model capability?
investigations.method: Compared the card against deterministic manifest/hash tools.
investigations.finding: No central model capability is evident.

history.reason: Rejected for hackathon feasibility; retained as a supported pain and negative control.

problems.title: Small-host UGC moderation misses advanced abuse

statement.user: Operators of small user-generated static-site hosting platforms
statement.task: Review each uploaded site for prohibited or harmful content
statement.failure: A simple phishing script misses advanced phishing and unsupported visual content, forcing manual review
statement.consequence: Review effort grows with uploads and missed abuse creates platform, legal, and user-safety risk

evidence.quote: this simple script does not catch some of the more advance phishing sites and it doesn't catch other types of content that we can't support on our platform like porn.
evidence.supports: Basic automation misses multiple abuse classes

evidence.quote: We're still going to be manually reviewing sites because we haven't reached a scale that makes that impossible.
evidence.supports: Manual review is the current fallback

counter_evidence: Safe Browsing, PhishTank, Spamhaus, and commercial NSFW classifiers may cover most common cases; baseline has not been run.

investigations.question: What does Safe Browsing plus NSFW detection miss on small static sites?
investigations.method: Run a labeled 20 phishing / 20 clean-site baseline and record false negatives, false positives, evidence quality, and cost.
investigations.next_action: Build the evaluation set before considering any new model.

history.reason: Residual gap is unmeasured; investigate against conventional baselines.

problems.title: Windows privacy settings may drift after updates

statement.task: Keep a desired privacy configuration across OS updates
statement.failure: Reports claim settings can revert, but frequency and causal attribution are disputed
statement.consequence: Users may repeatedly inspect settings or rely on scripts that become stale

evidence.quote: Many users find that after disabling certain settings, these settings are mysteriously re-enabled after updates or without apparent reason.
I've read so much FUD about Windows undoing settings with updates but in 3+ years it hasn't happened to me.
evidence.supports: The frequency of the problem is disputed

counter_evidence: ShutUp10, W10Privacy, Tripwire-style monitoring, and MDM baselines already address parts of the workflow.

investigations.question: Are there three independent post-24H2 reports with a KB, setting path, and reproducible revert?
investigations.method: Search issue trackers and Windows forums for reproducible reports.
investigations.next_action: Park unless independent evidence supports a specific residual gap.

history.reason: Supporting and counter evidence conflict; independent reproduction is missing.

problems.title: Third-party API changes are discovered only after user-facing breakage

statement.user: Teams maintaining many third-party production API integrations
statement.task: Keep integrations working as providers change APIs and behavior
statement.failure: At least one report describes silent breaking changes discovered only after users complained
statement.consequence: User-facing failures, reactive debugging, and uncertain integration health

evidence.quote: Recently worked on a project where our team used 10+ third-party APIs. Twice this year we got hit by silent breaking changes and found out only when users complained.
evidence.supports: A first-person report with a concrete integration count and frequency

evidence.quote: When node breaks their APIs, it breaks loaders using their APIs.
evidence.supports: A downstream project documents real breakage from upstream API changes

evidence.quote: Old versions of GL JS (<v2) remain publicly available via NPM and our CDN endpoints.
evidence.supports: Explicit versioning and retained old versions can mitigate breaking changes

counter_evidence: Lockfiles, contract tests, semantic versioning, provider changelogs, synthetic integration tests, Pact, and Schemathesis may already address the residual gap.

investigations.question: Can a reproducible silent API change evade pinning, contract tests, and changelog monitoring?
investigations.method: Construct or collect one changed API fixture and run the conventional baselines before considering any model.
investigations.next_action: Measure which baseline detects the change, detection lead time, and maintenance cost.

history.reason: Concrete first-person report plus independent downstream breakage evidence; residual gap remains unmeasured.

problems.title: Systematic-review screening misses buried eligibility evidence and requires repetitive extraction

statement.user: Researchers conducting systematic reviews and meta-analyses
statement.task: Find eligible studies and extract consistent fields across many papers
statement.failure: Relevant eligibility facts can be buried in full text or missed by search, while repeated extraction requires manual conversations or external scripts
statement.consequence: False exclusions, incomplete literature coverage, inconsistent extraction, and high reviewer time

evidence.quote: The sixth study was entirely new to me ... it's still something that my existing search processes missed
evidence.supports: A researcher reports missed relevant evidence during a meta-analysis search

evidence.quote: systematic literature reviews require applying the same analysis to dozens or even hunderds of papers
evidence.supports: Repeated analysis at review scale is a stated workflow burden

evidence.quote: It's becoming difficult to manage them all.
evidence.supports: A separate researcher reports literature-management difficulty

counter_evidence: Undermind, semantic scholarly search, Zotero, Rayyan, Covidence, ASReview, DistillerSR, and conventional database queries already address parts of discovery, screening, or extraction.

investigations.question: Do existing search and screening tools miss the same eligibility facts buried in full text, or is the gap only workflow inconvenience?
investigations.method: Use one published review protocol and labeled papers; compare conventional search, screening tools, and structured extraction against adjudicated decisions.
investigations.next_action: Measure recall, false exclusions, extraction agreement, citation traceability, and reviewer time before considering any model.

history.reason: Three independent reports describe literature-screening or management burden; residual gap and model necessity remain unmeasured.
